utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honour, good afternoon everyone in the courtroom. This is case IT-00-39-A, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now have the appearances of the parties and amicus. First for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Shelagh McCall. My co-counsel is Julia Thibord, and assisting is our case manager, Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. McCall. Mr. Krajisnik. Can you hear me in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, Judge, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik. You may sit down. Now, Mr. Dershowitz, we will be discussing your status a little bit later, but I see you in court and would you kindly acknowledge for the record that you're here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, my name is Alan Dershowitz, and I'm here in a limited capacity for Mr. Krajisnik as pursuant to the court's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dershowitz. You may sit down. Now as regarding the amicus, Mr. Nicholls, who will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Colin Nicholls as amicus together with Michelle Butler [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You will be participating by teleconferencing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Via teleconference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. I'm glad you are there and we will return to you later on. First, Mr. Krajisnik, I gather that the Registry received a motion from you late on Friday to allow Mr. Karganovic to be present today. I go not believe that I need to hear from the Prosecution on this motion. Now we are all aware of the fact that Mr. Karganovic has no official status in this case, but I will grant the motion on the understanding that he has no authority to make any submissions oral or otherwise during this proceeding. On this understanding and with no objection from the Prosecution, I suggest that Mr. Karganovic be invited to join Mr. Krajisnik in court. So now we have Mr. Karganovic here. Good afternoon, Mr. Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARGANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This as you know is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires the Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in the relations thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was heard on the 2nd of November, 2007. Although Rule 65 bis (B) required that the Status Conference be held on the 1st of March, the Appeals Chamber granted Mr. Krajisnik's request to postpone the Status Conference until today in order to allow Mr. Dershowitz to appear. I would like to begin this Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Krajisnik's health. Mr. Krajisnik, would you respond on this issue? Tell me how you have been doing physically and mentally.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge, sir. My health is good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm happy to hear that, and you -- before you sit down, Mr. Krajisnik, do you have any other concerns that you would like to raise pertaining to your well-being in the detention centre unit or nothing to say at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, as concerns that type of question and problem, I have nothing to add. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. We will be discussing other issues soon. Now, firstly I would like to recap for the parties where we are in terms of the briefing schedule. The English version of Mr. Krajisnik's appeal brief was filed on the 1st of February, and the Prosecution submitted the response on the 12th of March, 2008. Once Mr. Krajisnik has received a B/C/S translation of the response, hopefully within the next two weeks or so, he will then have 15 days under Rule 113 to submit a reply which may not exceed 9.000 words in length. Now, I would like to turn to the question of the supplementary brief by Mr. Dershowitz. In the decision of 28 February 2008, the Appeals Chamber granted leave for you, Mr. Dershowitz, acting as Mr. Krajisnik's counsel for a limited purpose to file a supplementary brief on behalf of Mr. Krajisnik relating only to the issue of the joint criminal enterprise. In its decision of 11 March 2008, the Appeals Chamber clarified that Mr. Dershowitz's submission should make clear the extent to which it complements or supersedes arguments that Mr. Krajisnik has already made in his appeal brief. Finally, on the 27th of March, 2008, the Appeals Chamber denied Mr. Krajisnik's motion to extend the briefing schedule. Let me note now that Mr. Krajisnik filed a power of attorney on Friday authorising Mr. Dershowitz to serve as his lawyer. The problem, however, is that that authorisation is very limited in scope, covering only today's Status Conference. Mr. Krajisnik, you must refile a power of attorney to indicate, I believe, that you are authorising Mr. Dershowitz to serve as your lawyer with respect to JCE issue and thus to make him -- to enable him to file the supplementary brief. Second, we must remember that Mr. Dershowitz himself has to file, if he has not done so yet, the appropriate paperwork with the Registry in order to serve as counsel before the Tribunal, and I would like to know, Mr. Dershowitz, whether you have already filed such paperwork in accordance with the decision of 28 February 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Krajisnik today filed the supplementary right of counsel, which I think the Registry now has, expanding my role pursuant to the Court's order, and we sent to the Court on Thursday by Federal Express all of the appropriate papers. It only arrived today at 1.47 p.m., but at about noontime I then refiled it in person and I'm now confident that the Court and the bar association have all the relevant papers, though I think the process of completing the certification has not been done as of 3.00 p.m. today but all the paperwork has been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm happy to hear that, Mr. Dershowitz, because of certain uncertainty whether the paperwork has already been completed to the extent that there will be any motions for Mr. Krajisnik today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: There will be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Krajisnik may have to submit them and I could suspend the meeting for a short time to enable you to assist him in preparing an oral motion if there is something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that would be necessary because we're not making a formal motion. What I would like to do is address the Court briefly. We have the consent of the Prosecution to seek from this Court a very, very brief delay in filing our limited brief. It is simply being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: How brief, Mr. Dershowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Well, the Court consents to a delay, and I quote: "Into early next week." So we would suggest April 8th, Tuesday or April 9th and that will not delay the appeal by a single day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I don't have that diary in front of me. Could you tell me what the date would be, say, Monday a week from now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Monday a week from now would be April 7th according to my calendar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And this is what you're asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: We ask for the 8th or the 9th and that's because the 8th or the 9th would result in not a single day of delay in all the papers being filed for this reason: As Your Honour noted, Mr. Krajisnik has two weeks from the time he gets the translation. As Your Honour noted, the translation will come hopefully in the next two weeks or so, and so we would then submit our brief and the government -- I'm sorry, the Prosecution's response 15 days later would come before Mr. Krajisnik's brief is due, which would result in not a single day of delay in the appellate proceeding, and that's why the Prosecution has consented and why we respectfully request that in our professional opinion it will take us that much time, particularly in light of the Court's order that we must reconcile everything we say with Mr. Krajisnik's brief and everything we say with the amicus brief as well. That has proved to be quite daunting, Your Honour, and there are also some new developments that Mr. Krajisnik might want to alert the Court to that we would like to incorporate into our response or into our brief under the joint criminal enterprise. But I think -- I know we can complete it. If the Court grants us until the 8th or the 9th, I know that we will not seek another delay. You have a representation from me on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I take it that this -- I'm only raising this because of a certain uncertainty about the completion of the paperwork. I take it that I can regard this motion, Mr. Krajisnik, as having been made by you and on your behalf, this motion for the extension of time which was requested by Mr. Dershowitz.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. I confirm that, and it's as you've just put it, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Do sit down, Mr. Krajisnik. So I have in front of me a new motion for an extension by about a week for the filing time. I must say that I'm not enthused about it. I thought that the time we granted was -- was more than enough for a person of Mr. Dershowitz's known talents and experience in drafting briefly complex papers on issues of criminal law and criminal procedure. You will recall that we allowed -- in allowing this supplementary brief, we did so on the condition that there would be a very strict briefing schedule and that we would avoid any details -- any delays. At present the normal briefing schedule should be completed around the middle of May. It is for this reason that the decision of 28th February imposed such a strict schedule, and it is also for this reason why the Appeals Chamber has largely denied both the Prosecution's and the Mr. Krajisnik's requests for extension. As Mr. Dershowitz points out today, however, I do recognise that the issues on which he will be drafting a supplementary brief are quite complex. Of course the issues that have been raised in the submissions by Mr. Dershowitz and Mr. Krajisnik regarding the difficulties with transfer of money and questions of private financing generally are beyond the purview of the Court, and of course I am well aware of the fact, and the Court is aware of the fact, that both Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Dershowitz learned on 29 February that the bank transfer had been blocked, yet did not file a motion for an extension until the 20th of March. On the 27th of March we denied this motion. But nevertheless, in the interests of justice, I would be prepared to grant in large part the motion made by Mr. Dershowitz, and I understand that the Prosecution does not have objections to this motion that he filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, on the basis that Mr. Dershowitz has set out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. McCall. I will grant you to the end of next Monday, Mr. Dershowitz.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, appreciate that very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I think it should resolve your problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: I think it will. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down now. This might be an appropriate moment before we turn to the Prosecution and to the amicus to ask Mr. Dershowitz whether he would like to raise or to make a statement on additional issues pertaining to that part of the appeal with regard to which he has been authorised to act for Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you very much. The Prosecution and I also agreed that as far as their brief is concerned, if their brief raises any new issues or issues that really require in the interests of justice a response, that we write a letter to the Court at that time and seek permission to file a letter or a supplementary brief within five days, not the usual 15. We have no expectation that we will have to do that, but we don't know for certain what the Prosecution's arguments will be, and if there are any arguments that we had not anticipated or arguments that require factual errors. So we would not ask the Court for anything but simply advice the Court that pursuant to the agreement with the Prosecution that if that becomes necessary, we will -- we will first negotiate with the Prosecution and then file a letter asking the Court for a number of days, just a brief number of days. And at that point we'll know better, too, whether or not it will delay the process any, and we would act in the spirit of this Court to make sure that the briefing schedule is not in any way delayed by our actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dershowitz. There is no need at this moment in time to anticipate difficulties. Should they arise we will look at that. Let me only make clear that the fact that the Defense and the Prosecution may have agreed among themselves on extensions, it would be not something which will be persuasive or certain, not conclusive for the Court which has its own interest in moving this appeal to a speedy resolution in the interests of justice and in the interests of your client.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So I'm not committing myself or the Court to how we would react should such a hypothetical request be made to us. Of course we will read it very carefully and consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: We appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Any other issues you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: At the moment there are no other issues. We are proceeding to write our brief. We will comply with the word limits and the time limits, and we appreciate both the Court and the Prosecution's reasonableness in pursuing the interests of justice. We all have the same goal, that is the quickest resolution of this matter in the interests of professionally being able to advise the Court to the best of our ability the complexity of the issue. So I just want to thank the Court and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, thank you for your comment, and I must add that I'm very happy to see you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm very happy to be here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Turning to the Prosecution are there any other issues -- I take it that the Defence has no further issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: May I confer with my client for one brief moment. Your Honour, Mr. Krajisnik has asked me to alert the Court and the Prosecution to the fact that he is preparing a Rule 115 motion that involves newly discovered evidence, videotapes and other matters that could not and were not available to the Court at the time of its judgement. My understanding is that these motions have a time schedule and they will be complied with. My only interest in that is to the extent that any of these matters relate to the joint criminal enterprise, I know at least one of them that does, I would be involved in that as well in advising Mr. Krajisnik and in submitting perhaps supplementary legal materials to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. We were -- we did anticipate some development of this kind and we in fact urged Mr. Krajisnik to act quickly on that, on those 115 motions, and we will look at them when they come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Maybe before turning to the Prosecution I would for a moment turn to the amicus if you agree. Mr. Nicholls, are you with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, we all know that the amicus has filed a motion seeking an opportunity to submit arguments regarding certain aspects of the Prosecution's response to Mr. Krajisnik's appeal brief specifically --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Specifically the amicus wishes to argue that the Appeals Chamber has discretion to deal with procedural irregularities, which he called procedural default, I believe, in a number of ways, from imposing sanctions to allowing irregularities to be cured. The Prosecution's response to this motion will be due on Friday, 4 April. We shall, of course, rule on your motion, Mr. Nicholls, as soon as possible after receiving the Prosecution's response. Is there anything that you would like to add at this juncture, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, there's nothing I would wish to add at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. You will still stay with us there, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Does the Prosecution have something to say with regard to just the point I raised with Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Simply to confirm, Your Honour, that we will be filing a response in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And you will be doing this by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krajisnik, do you have anything to add on this point? I suppose no because we have been to you a number of points -- times. Mr. Nicholls has no further issues, I gather, that you would like to raise. The Prosecution has anything?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just like to clarify one matter in relation to what Mr. Dershowitz says. As Your Honour is aware, there is no right of reply following the 28 February decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: And just to clarify the extent of the Prosecution's agreement it is that should he feel the need for some further filing that he would require to seek leave in order to do that, but the Prosecution hasn't committed itself about its attitude towards any such request should it come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's my understanding as well exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. In any event it's very clear that this will be submitted as a motion and we will decide upon it. We should not take anything for granted regarding the positions that the Court will take.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I think that we would have exhausted -- no. Ms. McCall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I'm very helpfully reminded by my co-counsel there is a sentence in the Prosecution's response brief in the introductory part that suggests that any paragraphs that the Prosecution thought should be summarily dismissed and were not dealt with in the body of the text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is in the context of the motion of Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. This is in the context of our response to Mr. Krajisnik's appeal brief that's been filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I see. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: There's a sentence that suggests that any paragraphs the Prosecution didn't deal with in the body of the text would appear at the end with a motion to summarily dismiss them. Can I say, Your Honour, that's -- that group of paragraphs didn't appear at the end, and I just want to clarify for Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Dershowitz that the Prosecution relies on the text of its response and there is a table annexed at the end that sets out all of Mr. Krajisnik's paragraph numbers and sets out where the Prosecution has responded. If any of Mr. Krajisnik's paragraph numbers have a blank space beside them, that means the Prosecution sees no need to respond and nothing more should be read into it than that. See just to clarify there may be some confusion between those two parts of the brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: So what exactly are you reserving your position then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. That was a previous matter. We would reserve our position on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: On the previous statement, not on this --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCCALL
utterances.text: On the previous issue about a further reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I believe that we have finished our agenda, and I thank you. I thank the staff. I thank the interpreters. I thank the parties, Mr. Dershowitz, Mr. Karganovic, Mr. Krajisnik for their participation. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: at 3.27 p.m.
